non_blocking: No published paper or preprint found that contains the main result (pooled pick-or-NONE vs isolated verification on all-wrong pools of officially graded MathArena solutions, with a criterion-shift/discriminability analysis). No ABANDON.

Closest prior art is wang2025llms (arXiv 2402.01349, COLING 2025). Its 'correct option replaced by None of the Above' setting and its finding that models 'opt for the least incorrect option' overlap the target-absent-pool premise. The paper acknowledges this and draws the contrast, but the Introduction and Contributions could say more plainly that the target-absent premise is not new for MCQ.

Related work could cite other adjacent preprints found: 2503.01550 (None of the Above, Less of the Right; already cited as tam2025none), 2509.20278 (Instruction Boundary: LLM behaviour when all options are wrong), 2603.04304 (V1: pointwise self-verification is biased toward accepting incorrect solutions, with pairwise as the fix; relevant to the isolated-vs-pooled contrast), and 2607.10139 (single-model self-scoring of candidates closes almost none of the oracle gap).

Related-work characterisations checked: the wang2025llms description (T/F verification of incorrect options, incorrect* confidence 83.6-99.4% of correct-option confidence on sub-datasets where the model predicts correctly, NOTA replacement) matches the arXiv full text. The accuracy of the ji2026candidate, zhang2026selected, rho2025best and ma2026selecting descriptions was not verified by me (zhang2026selected is flagged by the authors as abstract-only). The citation lens should confirm them.
The eyewitness framing is not itself novel to LLM judging, but no LLM paper using a lineup/target-absent design was found in several searches. This is absence of evidence, not proof.
evidence: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.01349 (text: 'options replaced by None of the above'; 'select the least incorrect option'; Table 3 confidence 83.6% to 99.4%)
https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.03417 (multi-sequence verifier, conditions on the full candidate set; not a lineup study)
